title: Abruzzo's Pumps Buck the National Trend
dek: Petrol runs half a cent below the Italian average while diesel quietly slips for the fourth day running.
body: Drivers filling up in Abruzzo today are paying €2.026 per litre for self-service Benzina and €2.162 for self-service Gasolio. That puts the region about four tenths of a cent below the national self-service average of €2.030 for petrol, while its diesel price sits just two tenths of a cent above the €2.160 nationwide figure — essentially at parity with the rest of the country.

The two fuels have been drifting in opposite directions locally over the past week: self-service Benzina crept up from €2.024 to €2.026 between August 25th and 31st, a slow but steady climb, while Gasolio eased back from €2.165 to €2.162 over the same stretch, its fourth straight daily dip. Abruzzo's station network stayed active throughout, with 603 of its 669 registered stations reporting prices today — a solid 90% turnout that points to consistent day-to-day coverage rather than any lapse in reporting.

A full week's trend line for a single region, broken down fuel by fuel, is only practical to publish every single day because Fuel Dashboard rebuilds itself automatically each morning straight from the national MIMIT feed. Nobody is re-pasting numbers into a spreadsheet — the pipeline was built with Claude Code and simply runs, region after region, which is what makes a rotating daily spotlight like Abruzzo's essentially free to produce.
pull_quote: Abruzzo's self-service diesel has eased for four straight readings, even as petrol keeps inching higher.
caption:
Today's regional spotlight on Fuel Dashboard: Abruzzo, where self-service petrol (€2.026/L) is running about half a cent below the Italian average, even as diesel (€2.162/L) sits almost exactly on the national line and has been easing for four days straight.

Fuel Dashboard tracks fuel prices across all 20 Italian regions every day, pulling directly from the Ministry's MIMIT feed and turning it into a self-updating, interactive site: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/. No spreadsheet, no manual data entry — just fresh numbers each morning.

That's really the point of this project. Building a daily, self-refreshing dashboard like this used to mean a dedicated data engineer or hours of manual spreadsheet upkeep. With Claude Code I built the whole pipeline — data ingestion, region-of-the-day logic, article generation, and the deployed site — as a side project, and it now maintains itself. It's a small but concrete example of how much more accessible AI tools have made building real, always-current products instead of a static, manually-updated Excel sheet.
